The Secretary-General's message reminds us that critical minerals do not create development on their own. The energy transition will be defined not only by what we extract from the ground, but by what we build above it.
 
Demand for key energy minerals has been growing by nearly 10% per year, with the energy sector accounting for around 75% of demand growth in 2025. Yet critical mineral investment declined by 9% last year, highlighting the need to translate growing demand into sustained investment throughout the value chain.
 
The opportunity extends beyond securing mineral supply. In Latin America and the Caribbean, for example, refining key energy minerals closer to where they are produced could increase the economic value generated by nearly 50% by 2035. Creating more value where minerals are produced is essential to turning mineral wealth into jobs, industrial development, economic diversification and long-term prosperity.
 
At UNDP , as co-chair of the Joint UN Task Force on Critical Energy Transition Minerals together with UN Environment Programme and UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) , we are supporting countries to strengthen governance, unlock sustainable investment, and build the policies and partnerships needed to translate mineral wealth into lasting development outcomes.
